title: Enhancing Multi Agent Large Language Models for Stock Trading through Quantitative Alpha Integration
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in algorithmic trading, yet knowledge integration across heterogeneous evidence remains underexplored in emerging and non-English markets. We present a five-agent knowledge-fusion framework for financial decision support in Vietnamese equities. The architecture integrates technical indicators, point-in-time quantitative alpha selection, financial sentiment, and vision-language chart analysis, providing a reproducible basis for combining heterogeneous quantitative, textual, and visual evidence in multi-agent reasoning. A paired shared report protocol isolates the contribution of alpha information while holding upstream evidence fixed, and a four-way ablation separates quantitative-factor and sentiment effects. Across nine equities and 180 paired decisions, the Full System attains 65.0% accuracy versus 51.1% without Alpha. The ablation identifies a larger independent contribution from alpha factors than from sentiment, with stock-dependent interactions. An execution-aware long-only ledger nevertheless produces a negative mean net return, showing that improved directional inference does not ensure economic profitability. The framework therefore supports auditable knowledge integration and controlled component evaluation for financial decision support; claims of immediate trading deployment remain outside the available evidence.
why: LLM agents on equities with ablations, but single market, accuracy not PnL, no costs.

title: Design and pricing of catastrophe bonds for pandemic risk transfer
abstract: Infectious disease outbreaks impose substantial fiscal burdens on governments, which bear the cost of the health emergency and the output lost to it while revenue is falling. Pandemic bonds offer a route to transferring part of that burden to capital markets, yet their effectiveness depends on accurate disease modelling and pricing. This study constructs two bond structures, per-occurrence and proportional, around a single observable prevalence trigger that requires no loss verification, so that settlement is fast enough to meet expenditure as it arises. Losses are quantified through an SVEI3RD compartmental model calibrated by a physics-informed neural network, with government costs modelled across mild, moderate and severe disease states alongside the labour production lost to illness, so the loss process captures the fiscal burden a government carries rather than death counts alone. A numerical hedging analysis calibrated to United States COVID-19 data shows both structures raise capital and reduce the government's pandemic loss. The per-occurrence bond commands a higher coupon, reflecting the total principal loss of its all-or-nothing payoff, whereas the proportional bond achieves greater variance reduction in net pandemic expenditure at the cost of a larger issuance. Neither design dominates, and the preferred structure depends on the issuer's risk preferences and capacity to fund nominal exposure. Sensitivity analysis shows that both coupons rise with the assumed pandemic frequency, the overall transmission level and the initial infection count, while faster waning immunity raises the proportional coupon alone. The proposed bonds offer a workable solution for governments preparing for future pandemics.
why: Pandemic cat bond pricing; PINN is epidemiology, not finance ML evaluation.

title: Evaluating Graph RAG vs. Vector RAG under Network Scaling, Topological Noise, and Financial Cost Constraints in Cross-Border Electrical Grid Cybersecurity
abstract: The ongoing digital transformation of critical energy infrastructures and theoperational interconnections of cross-border Smart Grids demand advancedautomated situational awareness and resilient threat intelligence frameworks.While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures are increasinglydeployed in Security Operations Centers (SOCs) for threat hunting andvulnerability management, standard dense vector retrieval (Vector RAG)struggles to capture multi-hop topological dependencies and complex attackpaths across interconnected IT/OT control systems. Conversely, KnowledgeGraph-structured retrieval (Graph RAG) preserves structural relationshipsbut introduces substantial computational, memory, and financial overheads.In this paper, we present an exhaustive quantitative benchmark comparingGraph RAG against Vector RAG across four network scaling tiers (Baseline,Medium, Large, and Mega), varying topological noise rates, and financialcost constraints within a cross-border electrical power grid spanning two nations. Our experimental findings demonstrate that Graph RAG substan-tially improves Context Recall over Vector RAG, maintaining 86.3%–100.0%across network scales compared to dropping below 3.8% for Vector RAG atMega scale. Furthermore, Graph RAG exhibits remarkable latency stability(0.86s–0.92s across all scale tiers) and robust resilience against topologicalnoise insertion. However, this analytical superiority introduces substantialoperational trade-offs: Graph RAG token consumption scales exponentiallyup to 2.70M tokens per query (an estimated cloud-equivalent cost of $6.75USD) at the Mega scale, whereas Vector RAG maintains a near-constant con-sumption of 262 tokens ($0.0007 USD). Finally, we synthesize these trade-offsand propose actionable architectural guidelines for deploying cost-effective,high-recall LLM solutions in critical infrastructure cybersecurity.
why: Grid cybersecurity RAG benchmark; finance is absent, not a finance paper.

title: A Deep Learning-Assisted Ratiometric Fluorescent Film Based on Carbon Dots and Naphthalimide Derivative for Visual Detection of Formaldehyde in Food Samples
abstract: The significant health risks posed by formaldehyde (FA) in food products call for rapid, sensitive, and on-site detection methods. In this work, we reported a ratiometric fluorescent film based on nitrogen-doped carbon dots (N-CD) and N-allyl-4-hydrazino-naphthalimide (AHNI) for the visual and intelligent detection of FA. AHNI selectively recognized FA via aldehyde-hydrazone condensation, which blocked PET and induced fluorescence enhancement with a red-shifted emission at 550 nm. Meanwhile, the N-CD served as a stable internal reference with a slight fluorescence decrease upon FA addition. Then, a smartphone-based portable device integrated with a 3D-printed detection box was constructed to capture fluorescence images and extract RGB values. Furthermore, the MobileNetV3-YOLOv5s (MV3-YOLOv5s) algorithm was employed to enhance recognition accuracy, achieving an overall accuracy of 0.993. The proposed sensing system exhibited excellent selectivity toward FA over various interfering species, with a detection limit as low as 0.163 µM. Satisfactory recoveries ranging from 97.5% to 102.8% were obtained in spiked food samples. This work provides a portable, cost-effective, and reliable strategy for on-site FA monitoring in food safety applications.
why: Fluorescent formaldehyde food detection; no finance or AI-in-finance content.
